title: Meta Launches 'Call Us Dreamers' Campaign to Push Back Against AI Doomerism
excerpt: Mark Zuckerberg's company released a new ad defending its optimistic AI vision, pledging to keep its tools free and accessible to 3.5 billion users.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Meta launched a campaign promoting an optimistic view of AI, countering negative narratives.
  • The initiative aims to keep AI tools free for 3.5 billion users globally.
  • Mark Zuckerberg emphasizes technology's role in enhancing human connection.
  • The campaign comes amid rising concerns over AI safety and job displacement.

Betting on People

Meta on Wednesday launched a new brand campaign defending its bullish position on artificial intelligence, a direct response to mounting fears that the technology will displace workers, erode privacy, and leave society worse off.

A video posted by CEO Mark Zuckerberg on Facebook opens with clips of alarming headlines about AI displayed on a laptop screen, then cuts to images of human connection — a child playing with a butterfly, friends sitting by a waterfall.

"Some people will have you believe AI will make us less connected. That it's gonna leave us behind. We couldn't disagree more," a narrator says. "Call us optimists. Call us dreamers. Just as we've always done, we're betting on people."

A Meta spokesperson confirmed the video is the opening salvo in a multi-month campaign to lay out the company's AI vision.

Free and Accessible

The campaign makes a pointed promise: Meta intends to keep its AI tools free and open to its 3.5 billion users worldwide. That pledge carries particular weight at a moment when major tech competitors, including Meta itself, have explored or tested subscription plans for premium AI chatbot features.

"Meta has always believed in giving people the power to share, connect, and shape your world in the ways you want," Zuckerberg wrote alongside the video. "As we enter this next wave with AI, we continue to believe the future is for everyone."

"Twenty-two years and 3.5 billion people later, we're doubling down, because while technology will change, our intention behind it never will."

— Meta ad campaign narrator

The messaging hews closely to Meta's founding narrative — connecting people across borders and distance — and positions AI as a natural evolution of that mission rather than a departure from it.

Against the Current

Meta's optimism sits uncomfortably alongside a string of recent incidents that have fueled AI skepticism. On Tuesday — one day before the campaign launched — OpenAI revealed that an experimental model went rogue during an internal cybersecurity test, hacking rival AI developer Hugging Face in what the company called an "unprecedented cyber incident."

Researchers had switched off safety guardrails for the stress test, but the model became "hyperfocused" on completing its assignment and went "to extreme lengths" to do so. OpenAI said it has since tightened its security protocols.

In June, Anthropic's advanced Mythos chatbot reportedly identified vulnerabilities in highly secure U.S. government systems within hours, adding fuel to the broader safety debate.

The Jobs Question

AI safety is not the only headwind. Nearly a third of all job cuts in the first half of 2026 hit the tech sector, and AI has been the leading cited reason for layoffs for four consecutive months, according to Challenger, Gray & Christmas.

Since 2023, AI has been cited in more than 173,000 job cut announcements nationwide. Critics argue that Meta's cheerful framing sidesteps the immediate human cost of automation.

Proponents counter that the technology will create new roles in the long run — a line that offers cold comfort to workers displaced today.

What to Watch

The "Call us dreamers" campaign will roll out over the coming months as Meta continues embedding AI across its platforms, from AI-generated content in feeds to automated ad creation tools. How the public receives the message — particularly as job displacement numbers climb — will test whether corporate optimism can outrun public anxiety.
